caller_preconditions.value: None beyond a reachable entry: no stack alignment, no memory map and no register input is required.

caller_supplied_registers.value: The callee reads no register. It loads two bytes from the BIOS image's own version area.

cpu_flag_handling.value: The two loads set N and Z from the loaded bytes. No compare or add is executed, so C and V are not written by the callee. I, D and T are not touched.

entry_address_and_basis.value: The reference image carries an 81 entry jump table at $E000 with 3 byte JMP entries. Slot $1E is at $E05A and jumps to a distinct internal routine in the same 8 KiB bank window.

executable_conditions_and_blocked_condit.value: Safe under the existing guarded probe: the callee has no side effect that the probe cannot contain. Execution is nevertheless blocked by the repository's reference JSR execution gate, which is closed for all 81 slots.

expected_return_value.value: X and Y carry the major and minor version bytes read from the image, so the value is a property of the private image and not a constant. A is left untouched.

interrupt_or_timing_dependence.value: The callee does not change the interrupt disable state, so the interrupt behaviour during the call is the caller's. With the interrupt disable flag set, which is how the guarded probe enters the callee, the core takes no maskable interrupt; the pinned core implements no NMI source either. A caller that enters with interrupts enabled would not get that guarantee.

mpr_change.value: No MPR is read or written.

possibly_changed_registers.value: X and Y only. A is not written by the callee.

ram_io_vdc_cd_side_effects.value: No store of any kind, no VDC access, no CD access and no I/O page access. The only reads are two bytes inside the API bank window.

stack_usage.value: The callee pushes nothing. The caller's JSR occupies two stack bytes and the callee's RTS releases them, so the stack is balanced.

caller_preconditions.value: A is expected to be 0..99. The routine compares A against 100 and returns immediately when A is 100 or larger, so the out of range behaviour is observable rather than undefined.

caller_supplied_registers.value: The callee reads A as the binary input and compares it against 100. X is used as a scratch counter. Y is not read and not written by the callee.

cpu_flag_handling.value: A compare against 100 precedes the conversion, so C carries the comparison result on the early return path. The conversion itself ends with a carry clear. The remaining flags are not established.

entry_address_and_basis.value: Slot $3C is at $E0B4 in the confirmed 3 byte JMP jump table and jumps to a distinct internal routine in the API bank window.

executable_conditions_and_blocked_condit.value: The single store lands in page 1 and therefore inside the RAM write allowlist of the existing guarded probe, so the probe would contain it. The store does clobber the System Card zero page area, so a caller must not keep live data there across the call. Execution is blocked by the reference JSR execution gate.

expected_return_value.value: The packed BCD result and the out of range signalling are not established. The static analysis shows a compare against 100, a decimal conversion loop and a return, but it does not establish the returned value or the flag contract.

interrupt_or_timing_dependence.value: The callee does not change the interrupt disable state, so the interrupt behaviour during the call is the caller's. With the interrupt disable flag set, which is how the guarded probe enters the callee, the core takes no maskable interrupt; the pinned core implements no NMI source either. A caller that enters with interrupts enabled would not get that guarantee.

mpr_change.value: No MPR is read or written.

possibly_changed_registers.value: A and X are written. Y is not written by the callee.

ram_io_vdc_cd_side_effects.value: Exactly one store, to a zero page byte. The HuC6280 zero page is at $2000, so under the pinned core and on hardware alike the store lands in page 1, not in the memory mapped I/O page. No VDC, CD or I/O access occurs.

stack_usage.value: One byte is pushed and released by the callee; the caller's JSR occupies two more. The stack is balanced.

caller_supplied_registers.value: The callee reads A as the packed BCD input and masks it into two nibbles, which it then tests against 10.

cpu_flag_handling.value: A compare against $A0 tests the high nibble and a compare against 10 tests the low nibble, so C carries the digit test result on the early return path. The remaining flags are not established.

entry_address_and_basis.value: Slot $3D is at $E0B7 in the confirmed 3 byte JMP jump table and jumps to a distinct internal routine in the API bank window.

executable_conditions_and_blocked_condit.value: Both stores land in page 1 and are therefore inside the probe's RAM write allowlist, but they clobber the System Card zero page area. Execution is blocked by the reference JSR execution gate.

expected_return_value.value: The binary result and the invalid digit signalling are not established. The static analysis shows the nibble tests and a return, but not the returned value or the flag contract.

interrupt_or_timing_dependence.value: The callee does not change the interrupt disable state, so the interrupt behaviour during the call is the caller's. With the interrupt disable flag set, which is how the guarded probe enters the callee, the core takes no maskable interrupt; the pinned core implements no NMI source either. A caller that enters with interrupts enabled would not get that guarantee.

ram_io_vdc_cd_side_effects.value: Exactly two stores, both to zero page bytes, so both land in page 1 on the HuC6280. No VDC, CD or I/O access occurs.

stack_usage.value: One byte is pushed and released by the callee; the caller's JSR occupies two more. The stack is balanced.
